contract.provides: Source-reported global theorem candidate: distinct canonical-sign nonidentity Pauli strings P_a on n qubits, support size <=k and candidate incidence max_i #{a:i in supp P_a}<=Delta (including zero-coefficient candidates), H(h)=sum h_a P_a with max_i sum_(a:i in supp P_a)|h_a|<=g, beta>0 and an unrestricted full-rank Gibbs state rho_h. For every real u, A=sum u_aP_a and A_c=A-Tr(rho A)I, the manuscript proposes centered KMS norm squared >=c||u||_2^2 and therefore BKM covariance >=c||u||_2^2, c=exp[-C_(k,Delta)(1+beta g)^2]. C is finite/constructive, independent of n,m, signs, gaps and mixing, but potentially extremely conservative. No commutation, frustration exclusion, high temperature or correlation-decay assumption is made. This is an unreviewed derivation with unknown independent correctness/priority, not a validated new physical law or end-to-end learning advantage.
